claims.reason: Classified as an editors' caveat that narrows what the item's advice covers. No snapshot says which digital programmes qualify: the European abstract says only 'digitally', the NHS says 'online self-help programme', and AASM says there was insufficient evidence to make recommendations for specific delivery methods. scope_gaps.note: Digital delivery is backed by the European guideline abstract ('in-person or digitally') and the NHS page, not by AASM: AASM says there was insufficient evidence to make recommendations for specific delivery methods (line 294) and that its strong CBT-I recommendation rests primarily on professional-delivered CBT-I (line 300). No snapshot defines what an 'odpowiedni' digital programme is.

The sentence describes the evidence base as review-based clinical recommendations; the European guideline's method is not visible in the abstract-only snapshot, and the NHS page is patient information.
The sentence states benefit-risk weighing as a general condition; the abstract states it only for longer-term treatment.
